did_you_know.text: The chapter opens with “the burden of the word of the LORD concerning Israel” and presents the LORD as the one who stretches out the heavens, lays the foundations of the earth, and forms the human spirit within each person.
Jerusalem is described as a “cup of staggering” to all the surrounding nations, and Judah is also mentioned as being under siege against Jerusalem.
Jerusalem is called a “burdensome stone” for all the nations: whoever tries to lift it will be severely injured, and all the nations of the earth will gather against it.
The LORD describes the defeat of the enemy’s military strength: the horses will be struck with panic and blindness, and their riders with madness.
The leaders of Judah will recognize that their strength comes from the inhabitants of Jerusalem, who rely on the LORD of hosts, their God.
The leaders of Judah are compared to a blazing fire among pieces of wood and to a flaming torch among sheaves—images expressing their ability to overcome the surrounding nations.
The LORD promises to save the tents of Judah first, so that the glory of David’s house and the glory of Jerusalem’s inhabitants will not surpass that of Judah.
The LORD will protect the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and even the weakest among them will be like David, a warrior; the house of David will be like God, like the angel of the LORD leading them.

A spirit of grace and supplication will be poured out on the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem. They will look toward the one who was pierced and mourn for him as for a beloved only son or a firstborn.
Mourning will spread throughout the land by families, with the families of David, Nathan, Levi, and Shimei mentioned especially; the men and women will mourn separately.
